dedupe_keys.name: geese global earthquake scenarios rupture and ground motion scenario database

description: GEESE is both an algorithm and a database. The algorithm retrieves representative finite ruptures (size, geometry and orientation) for queried earthquakes from seismic hazard models built for the OpenQuake Engine, and the database applies it to the strongest events of the global ISC-GEM earthquake catalogue from 1904 to 2019. For each event with a matched rupture the database gives the inputs for an OpenQuake hazard scenario calculation and ground-motion fields computed with reconfigurable default parameters. It was built by Christopher Brooks, Marco Pagani, Manuela Villani, Kendra Johnson, Richard Styron and Kirsty Bayliss at the GEM Foundation and described in an open-access article in Seismica (2025) on source model testing and rapid post-event response. Version 1 of 6 March 2025 is accessible on Zenodo as one free zip file of about 7 GB under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: ruptures are matched from hazard models, not observed, ground-motion fields use default parameters, and commercial use needs another licence. It supports scenario-based damage and cascading impact simulation of infrastructure for historical earthquakes and rapid post-event analysis; related records are the OpenQuake Engine and the GEM Global Seismic Hazard Map.
